notes: Job list for tools/render/render-short.mjs. `node render-short.mjs --list` prints it with indexes.
kind "video" records a clip at `size` for `seconds`; kind "pin" grabs a single 1000x1500 still.
caption is trimmed to 80 characters by render.html; sub is the small line under the circle.
technique is a key from js/techniques.js: 478, box, coherent, sigh, extended, triangle, wim.
url is the page the post should link to. pinDescription is what you paste into Pinterest.
defaults.audio is resolved from the repo root. audio/ holds our own CC0 beds (drone, rain,
ocean, night, forest, brown-noise) — swap the file per job with an "audio" field. If the file
is missing, or ffmpeg cannot handle audio, the clip gets a silent stereo track instead.
Optional per-job fields: "theme" (palette override), "phrase": false (hide the engine sentence),
"poseMs" (pins only — how long to wait so the circle is caught mid-inhale).

jobs.caption: One minute of slow breathing, anywhere
4-7-8 for the 2 a.m. wake-up
jobs.sub: In for four. Hold for seven. Out for eight.
jobs.pinDescription: The 4-7-8 pattern is simple to remember at 2 a.m.: breathe in through the nose for four, hold for seven, breathe out through the mouth for eight. This guided timer counts it for you, so you can follow a circle instead of counting in your head. Optional sound and vibration cues, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/4-7-8-breathing

jobs.caption: How 4-7-8 breathing actually goes
jobs.sub: Four in. Seven hold. Eight out. Four rounds.
jobs.pinDescription: Four counts in, seven counts holding, eight counts out — four rounds is a normal place to start. Start seated, and skip the hold entirely if holding your breath makes you uneasy. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow and optional audio cues. https://helpmebreath.com/4-7-8-breathing

jobs.caption: Put 4-7-8 at the end of your bedtime routine
jobs.pinDescription: Teeth, alarm, lights off, then four rounds of 4-7-8 in bed. Keeping it in the same place every night makes it easier to remember than deciding to do it when you are already awake at 3 a.m. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: Stop counting in your head
jobs.sub: Let the circle hold the count
jobs.pinDescription: Counting 4-7-8 in your head is one more thing to keep track of. Follow a circle instead: it grows on the in-breath, holds, and shrinks on the out-breath. Free guided breathing timer with optional sound and vibration cues. https://helpmebreath.com/4-7-8-breathing

jobs.caption: If the seven-count hold feels like too much
jobs.sub: Shorten it. The rhythm still works.
jobs.pinDescription: A seven-count hold is uncomfortable for a lot of people, and holding your breath is not for everyone. Shorten the hold, or drop it and simply make the out-breath longer than the in-breath. Guided timer, three sessions free with seven patterns to try. https://helpmebreath.com/4-7-8-breathing

jobs.caption: Save this for tonight
jobs.pinDescription: A guided 4-7-8 timer: in for four, hold for seven, out for eight, with a circle to follow and optional audio cues. Free to try, three sessions before you sign in; no app to install, and it works offline once the page has loaded. https://helpmebreath.com/4-7-8-breathing

jobs.caption: Box breathing before the meeting
jobs.sub: Four in, four hold, four out, four hold
jobs.pinDescription: Box breathing is four equal counts: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Four sides, one square. It is easy to do in a chair with your eyes open, which is why it survives meetings. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing

jobs.caption: A four-count reset without leaving your desk
jobs.pinDescription: One round of box breathing is sixteen seconds. You can do it between two tabs without anyone noticing. In for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: What box breathing actually is
jobs.sub: Equal counts on all four sides
jobs.pinDescription: Box breathing keeps every part of the breath the same length: in, hold, out, hold. Start at four counts and shorten to three if four feels long. Guided timer, three sessions free with optional sound and vibration cues. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing

jobs.caption: Box breathing before you have to speak
jobs.pinDescription: Before you present, before the call, before the difficult conversation: two or three rounds of box breathing while you wait. Four in, four hold, four out, four hold. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing

jobs.caption: A breathing break between study blocks
jobs.pinDescription: Between study blocks, one or two rounds of box breathing gives you a break that does not turn into twenty minutes of scrolling. In for four, hold, out for four, hold. Guided timer, free to try, three sessions before you sign in. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: Box breathing or 4-7-8?
jobs.sub: One is even. One leans on the out-breath.
jobs.pinDescription: Box breathing keeps all four counts equal, which makes it easy to do with your eyes open. 4-7-8 puts the weight on a long out-breath, which suits lying down. A side-by-side comparison with a timer for each, so you can try both on one page. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing-vs-4-7-8

jobs.caption: Six breaths a minute
jobs.sub: Five seconds in, five seconds out
jobs.pinDescription: Coherent breathing is five seconds in and five seconds out — about six breaths a minute, roughly half the usual rate. There is nothing to hold and nothing to count past five. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow and optional audio cues. https://helpmebreath.com/heart-coherence-breathing

jobs.caption: Ten slow minutes, twice a day
jobs.sub: Five in, five out, nothing held
jobs.pinDescription: Slow breathing is usually practised in longer sits — ten minutes at a time — rather than as a one-off. This timer runs five seconds in, five seconds out, with session lengths from three to twenty minutes. It is not a substitute for medical care or prescribed treatment. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-high-blood-pressure

jobs.caption: Slow breathing with nothing to hold
jobs.pinDescription: If breath-holds make you uneasy, coherent breathing has none: five seconds in, five seconds out, over and over. It is the gentlest pattern on the site. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/heart-coherence-breathing

jobs.caption: A quiet breath on the way home
jobs.pinDescription: On the bus, in the passenger seat, on the walk from the station: five seconds in, five seconds out. Nothing to hold, nothing to count past five. Free guided breathing timer with optional sound and vibration cues. https://helpmebreath.com/heart-coherence-breathing

jobs.caption: Five in, five out, until the day lets go
jobs.pinDescription: A slow, even rhythm for the end of the day: five seconds in, five seconds out. Follow the circle rather than counting. Guided timer with seven patterns, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/heart-coherence-breathing

jobs.caption: Two breaths in, one long breath out
jobs.pinDescription: Cyclic sighing is a double inhale through the nose — a full breath, then a short top-up — followed by a long, slow out-breath through the mouth. It has the shape of a sigh. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/cyclic-sighing

jobs.caption: The shape of a sigh, on purpose
jobs.sub: Sip, top up, let it all go
jobs.pinDescription: Two inhales through the nose, then one long exhale through the mouth — the shape a sigh already has. Cyclic sighing does it deliberately, on a count. Guided timer with optional sound cues, free to try, three sessions before you sign in. https://helpmebreath.com/cyclic-sighing

jobs.caption: A quiet minute after hard news
jobs.sub: Two in through the nose, one long out
jobs.pinDescription: When something lands badly, a few cycles of two-in, one-long-out gives you something simple to do with your body while the rest of you catches up. Free guided breathing timer with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: A reset in the middle of a night shift
jobs.pinDescription: Short enough for a corridor, quiet enough for a break room: two breaths in through the nose, one long breath out through the mouth. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline once the page has loaded. https://helpmebreath.com/cyclic-sighing

jobs.caption: Three counts in, three hold, three out
jobs.pinDescription: Triangle breathing has three equal sides: in for three, hold for three, out for three. One round is nine seconds, which makes it the easiest pattern to actually finish. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/triangle-breathing

jobs.caption: Triangle breathing while you wait in line
jobs.sub: Nobody can tell you are doing it
jobs.pinDescription: Three in, three hold, three out. Eyes open, nothing visible from the outside, nine seconds a round. Guided breathing timer with optional sound and vibration cues, three sessions free. https://helpmebreath.com/triangle-breathing

jobs.caption: A three-count breath a child can follow
jobs.sub: Trace a triangle with the breath
jobs.pinDescription: Three counts is short enough for a child to hold on to: in for three, hold for three, out for three, tracing one side of a triangle each time. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow on screen. https://helpmebreath.com/triangle-breathing

jobs.caption: Waiting-room breathing
jobs.pinDescription: For appointments, results and the twenty minutes before them: in for three, hold for three, out for three. Free guided breathing timer, no sign-up, nothing stored about you. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: A faster rhythm for a slow morning
jobs.sub: Sit or lie down first. Never in or near water.
jobs.pinDescription: Energizing breath is a faster, rhythmic pattern — quick in, quick out. Always practise seated or lying down, never in or near water, and stop if you feel light-headed. Not for pregnancy, cardiovascular conditions, uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy or recent surgery. Guided timer, three sessions free with a safety check before it starts. https://helpmebreath.com/energizing-breath

jobs.caption: Read this before fast breathing
jobs.sub: Seated only, never in or near water. Stop if you feel light-headed.
jobs.pinDescription: Fast breathing patterns are not for everyone. Never do them in or near water, never while driving, and skip them entirely during pregnancy or with cardiovascular conditions, uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy, respiratory conditions or recent surgery. The guided timer asks you to confirm you have read this before it will start. https://helpmebreath.com/energizing-breath

jobs.caption: Before you reach for the third coffee
jobs.sub: Seated, never in or near water, two minutes
jobs.pinDescription: A short, faster breathing pattern you do sitting down, never in or near water. Two minutes, then back to work. Read the safety notes first — it is the one pattern on the site that carries real contraindications. Guided timer with a safety check before it starts. https://helpmebreath.com/energizing-breath

jobs.caption: Breathe out longer than you breathe in
jobs.pinDescription: If you remember one thing about breathing when you are anxious, make it this: let the out-breath run longer than the in-breath. Four in, six out is a good starting ratio. Free guided timer with a circle to follow, no account, no ads on this page. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: One slow minute when anxiety spikes
jobs.pinDescription: One minute, one pattern, nothing to hold: breathe in for four, out for six. A free guided timer counts it for you. If you are in crisis, please contact a local crisis line — the page lists them at the top. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: Five slow patterns for anxious moments
jobs.sub: Pick the one you can actually follow
jobs.pinDescription: Extended exhale, cyclic sighing, coherent breathing, triangle and box — five slow patterns, each with a guided timer on the page, so you can find the one you can follow when you are not calm. Free, no account, no ads on this page. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: For Sunday-evening dread
jobs.sub: Breathe out longer than you breathe in
jobs.pinDescription: The Sunday-evening version of anxiety is quiet and long. Four counts in, six counts out, for as long as you want to sit with it. Free guided breathing timer with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: When your hands will not stop shaking
jobs.pinDescription: Two breaths in through the nose, one long breath out through the mouth, repeated. Something simple to do with your body while the rest of you settles. Free guided timer, no sign-up. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: Anxious at your desk, eyes open
jobs.sub: Three in, three hold, three out
jobs.pinDescription: You do not have to close your eyes or leave the room. Three counts in, three holding, three out, for a minute. Free guided breathing timer with optional sound and vibration cues. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: Do not try to take a bigger breath
jobs.pinDescription: When anxiety climbs, the instinct is to pull in more air. Try aiming at the out-breath instead: same in-breath, longer out. Free guided timer with a circle that shows you the ratio. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-anxiety

jobs.caption: Ten slow breaths before you close your eyes
jobs.pinDescription: Four counts in, seven holding, eight out, ten times, already lying down with the lights off. A guided timer counts it so you do not have to. Three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: Wind down without a screen in your hand
jobs.pinDescription: Set the timer, put the phone face-down beside you, and follow the sound cues instead of the screen. Four counts in, six counts out. Free guided breathing timer with optional audio and vibration. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: The 3 a.m. wake-up plan
jobs.pinDescription: Decide the pattern before you need it. At 3 a.m. you will not choose well. 4-7-8 or a simple long out-breath, ten rounds, eyes closed. Guided timer, three sessions free with seven patterns and session lengths from three minutes. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: When your mind will not stop at night
jobs.sub: Four in, seven hold, eight out
jobs.pinDescription: Counting the breath gives a busy mind something dull to hold on to. Four in, seven hold, eight out. The timer keeps the count so you can let it go. Three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: Quiet enough for a sleeping partner
jobs.sub: Five in, five out, no sound needed
jobs.pinDescription: Nothing to hold, nothing audible: five seconds in through the nose, five seconds out. Turn the cues off and follow the circle, or set vibration only. Free guided breathing timer. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: Sleeping when the world is awake
jobs.pinDescription: For daytime sleep after a night shift: a slow, even pattern with nothing to hold, run for ten or twenty minutes. Guided timer, three sessions free with session lengths up to twenty minutes and an unlimited option. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: Put the breathing last
jobs.pinDescription: It is easier to keep as the last thing you do, rather than something you fit in before brushing your teeth. Lights off, phone down, then four in and six out. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-sleep

jobs.caption: The first minute of a panic wave
jobs.pinDescription: Something to do in the first minute: aim only at the out-breath — in for four, out for six, nothing held. A free guided timer counts it for you. This page carries crisis-line numbers at the top and has no ads. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-panic-attacks

jobs.caption: Something steady to follow in a panic
jobs.sub: Three in, three hold, three out
jobs.pinDescription: When thinking is hard, a nine-second shape is easier to follow than a long pattern. Three in, three hold, three out, with a circle on screen. Free, no account, no ads on this page. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-panic-attacks

jobs.caption: If holding your breath makes it worse
jobs.sub: Five in, five out, nothing held
jobs.pinDescription: Breath-holds are not for everyone, and plenty of people would rather not hold their breath at all when they are frightened. Coherent breathing has none: five seconds in, five seconds out. Free guided timer with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-panic-attacks

jobs.caption: Decide your pattern before you need it
jobs.pinDescription: It is hard to choose a breathing pattern in the middle of a panic wave. Pick one now, practise it when you are calm, and it will be there later. Free guided timer with seven patterns. Crisis-line numbers are listed at the top of the page. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-panic-attacks

jobs.caption: Breathing with someone who is panicking
jobs.pinDescription: Say the counts out loud and breathe with them rather than telling them to calm down. Three in, three hold, three out. Free guided timer you can hold up so you are both following the same circle. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-panic-attacks

jobs.caption: Box breathing before deep work
jobs.pinDescription: Two rounds of box breathing before you start, as a way of marking the beginning of the block. In for four, hold, out for four, hold. Guided timer, three sessions free, works offline. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: One box round between two tasks
jobs.pinDescription: One round of box breathing is sixteen seconds — short enough that you will actually do it between two tasks instead of opening another tab. Free guided breathing timer with a circle to follow. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: Nine seconds. That is the whole thing.
jobs.sub: Three in, three hold, three out
jobs.pinDescription: The shortest pattern on the site: one triangle round is nine seconds. Use it as a full stop between two pieces of work. Guided timer, three sessions free with optional sound and vibration cues. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: The 3 p.m. slump, without more caffeine
jobs.pinDescription: Five seconds in, five seconds out, for three minutes, away from the screen. Nothing to hold and nothing to count past five. Guided breathing timer, free to try, three sessions before you sign in. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: A breathing break between study blocks
jobs.pinDescription: Two rounds of box breathing at the end of each study block gives the break a shape and a stopping point. In for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Guided timer, three sessions free. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-focus

jobs.caption: Slow breathing, ten minutes, twice a day
jobs.pinDescription: A free timer for slow breathing at about six breaths a minute: five seconds in, five seconds out, for ten minutes. The page sets out what the research does and does not show. This is not a treatment and it does not replace medication or medical advice. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-high-blood-pressure

jobs.caption: What slow breathing does and does not show
jobs.pinDescription: A plain summary of what the research on slow breathing and blood pressure actually reports, including where the evidence is weak. Never stop or change prescribed medication because of a breathing exercise — talk to your doctor. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-high-blood-pressure

jobs.caption: Take this to your next appointment
jobs.sub: Five in, five out, ten minutes
jobs.pinDescription: If you want to add slow breathing to what you already do, say so at your next appointment rather than changing anything on your own. Guided timer, three sessions free with session lengths from three to twenty minutes. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-high-blood-pressure

jobs.caption: Slow breathing for a loud afternoon
jobs.sub: Five seconds in, five seconds out
jobs.pinDescription: Ten minutes, seated, five seconds in and five seconds out. Guided timer, three sessions free with a circle to follow and optional audio cues. Not a substitute for medical care. https://helpmebreath.com/breathing-exercises-for-high-blood-pressure

jobs.caption: Box breathing or 4-7-8?
jobs.sub: Try both on the same page
jobs.pinDescription: Box breathing keeps four equal counts and works with your eyes open. 4-7-8 leans on a long out-breath and suits lying down. A side-by-side comparison with a working timer for each, so you can try both before deciding. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing-vs-4-7-8

jobs.caption: Which breathing pattern should you use?
jobs.sub: It depends on where you are
jobs.pinDescription: Sitting in a meeting, lying in bed, standing in a queue — the situation decides the pattern more than the pattern decides the result. A short comparison with a timer for each, free to try, three sessions before you sign in. https://helpmebreath.com/box-breathing-vs-4-7-8

jobs.caption: What the research actually says
jobs.pinDescription: A plain-language summary of the published research behind slow breathing, with links to the primary sources and honest notes on where the evidence is thin. No claims that breathing treats or cures anything. https://helpmebreath.com/science

jobs.caption: Seven guided breathing patterns, three sessions free
jobs.sub: Pick one, set a length, follow the circle
jobs.pinDescription: One timer, seven patterns: 4-7-8, box, coherent, cyclic sighing, extended exhale, triangle and energizing breath. Audio and vibration cues, session lengths from three minutes, and it keeps working offline. Three sessions free before you sign in. https://helpmebreath.com/timer
